root_cause: The design still retires correctly (no trace mismatches and no timeout), so this is an issue/control performance bug rather than a datapath error. While an older load is held in the LSU waiting on the external-memory handshake, younger independent ALU instructions are never allowed to enter/leave the issue path and complete, so dbg_ooo_bypass can never qualify. The most likely location is the per-instruction dispatch-ready selection in rename_unit, where a global LSU-ready/load-pending condition can block non-memory dispatch; if dispatch is already type-correct, the same symptom can come from issue selection being gated by the ROB head/load-pending state or from the ROB not accepting a younger ALU completion while the older load is outstanding.

Keep the external memory handshake correct: at most one outstanding request, valid/address held until ready, and no retraction on flush or halt.
dbg_ooo_issue and dbg_ooo_bypass must be single-cycle events derived from real issue/completion state, at most one per instruction per cycle, never from counters or PC patterns.
Preserve the landed rename FIFO/bitmap refactor and keep checkpoint 2D-array writes constant-row-index (row-decoded) for synthesis; do not introduce other variable-index writes into unpacked arrays.
